name: Software Requirements
practice_prompt: Coach the student to draft requirements for a campus food-ordering app. Follow: end-in-mind → functional → non-functional → testable examples. Nudge if they jump ahead. One piece at a time.

practice_stages.label: end in mind
practice_stages.focus: Clarify what we're producing — key requirements for a campus food app. Ask what problems it should solve.

practice_stages.label: functional requirements
practice_stages.focus: Draft 1–2 functional requirements. Ask the student what users must be able to do.

practice_stages.label: non-functional requirements
practice_stages.focus: Draft 1–2 non-functional requirements (performance, security, etc.). Ask how the system should behave.

practice_stages.label: testable examples
practice_stages.focus: Make one requirement testable — clear, measurable acceptance. Ask how they'd verify it.

final_example: Sample: Functional — 'Student can browse menus by dining hall.' Non-functional — 'App loads menu in under 2 seconds on campus Wi-Fi.'
check_questions: What is the difference between functional and non-functional requirements?
Give one example of each for any app you know.
Why do we write an SRS before coding?
What makes a requirement 'good' or testable?
